queries.title: Are premium players worth the money? Points per £m by position and price band. Only counts players who played meaningful minutes (900+ in the season).
queries.sql:
-- Q: Are premium players worth the money? Points per £m by position and price band.
-- Only counts players who played meaningful minutes (900+ in the season).
WITH season_totals AS (
    SELECT g.season, g.player_id, p.position,
           SUM(g.points)  AS points,
           SUM(g.minutes) AS minutes,
           AVG(g.price)   AS avg_price
    FROM player_gw g
    JOIN players p ON p.season = g.season AND p.player_id = g.player_id
    WHERE p.position <> 'AM'
    GROUP BY g.season, g.player_id, p.position
    HAVING SUM(g.minutes) >= 900
)
SELECT position,
       CASE WHEN avg_price < 5.0 THEN '1: under 5.0'
            WHEN avg_price < 6.5 THEN '2: 5.0-6.4'
            WHEN avg_price < 8.5 THEN '3: 6.5-8.4'
            ELSE '4: 8.5+' END                         AS price_band,
       COUNT(*)                                        AS player_seasons,
       ROUND(AVG(points), 1)                           AS avg_season_points,
       ROUND(AVG(points / avg_price), 2)               AS points_per_million,
       ROUND(AVG(90.0 * points / minutes), 2)          AS points_per_90
FROM season_totals
GROUP BY position, price_band
ORDER BY position, price_band;

queries.title: Which low-owned players returned the most points each season?  The data gives ownership as a raw count of managers, not a percentage. Every FPL squad holds exactly 15 players, so for any gameweek: total managers ~= SUM(selected_by over all players) / 15 which lets us turn counts into ownership %.
queries.sql:
-- Q: Which low-owned players returned the most points each season?
--
-- The data gives ownership as a raw count of managers, not a percentage.
-- Every FPL squad holds exactly 15 players, so for any gameweek:
--     total managers ~= SUM(selected_by over all players) / 15
-- which lets us turn counts into ownership %.
WITH managers_per_gw AS (
    SELECT season, gw, SUM(selected_by) / 15.0 AS managers
    FROM player_gw
    GROUP BY season, gw
),
ownership AS (
    SELECT g.season, g.player_id, g.points, g.price,
           100.0 * g.selected_by / m.managers AS ownership_pct
    FROM player_gw g
    JOIN managers_per_gw m ON m.season = g.season AND m.gw = g.gw
),
totals AS (
    SELECT o.season, p.web_name, p.position,
           SUM(o.points)        AS points,
           AVG(o.price)         AS avg_price,
           AVG(o.ownership_pct) AS avg_ownership_pct
    FROM ownership o
    JOIN players p ON p.season = o.season AND p.player_id = o.player_id
    GROUP BY o.season, o.player_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season ORDER BY points DESC) AS rn
    FROM totals
    WHERE avg_ownership_pct < 5.0
)
SELECT season, web_name, position, points,
       ROUND(avg_price, 1)         AS avg_price,
       ROUND(avg_ownership_pct, 1) AS avg_ownership_pct
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 5
ORDER BY season, points DESC;

queries.title: Is "form" real? If a player averaged X points over his last 5 gameweeks, what does he actually score next? Compared with what his season-long average predicts. Restricted to regular starters so we measure form, not rotation.
queries.sql:
-- Q: Is "form" real? If a player averaged X points over his last 5 gameweeks,
-- what does he actually score next? Compared with what his season-long average predicts.
-- Restricted to regular starters so we measure form, not rotation.
SELECT CASE WHEN points_l5 < 2 THEN '1: under 2'
            WHEN points_l5 < 4 THEN '2: 2-4'
            WHEN points_l5 < 6 THEN '3: 4-6'
            WHEN points_l5 < 8 THEN '4: 6-8'
            ELSE '5: 8+' END                    AS last5_avg_band,
       COUNT(*)                                 AS player_gameweeks,
       ROUND(AVG(points_l5), 2)                 AS avg_last5,
       ROUND(AVG(points_std), 2)                AS avg_season_to_date,
       ROUND(AVG(target_points), 2)             AS avg_next_gw_points
FROM player_features
WHERE gws_so_far >= 8
  AND starts_l5 >= 0.8
  AND position <> 'AM'
GROUP BY last5_avg_band
ORDER BY last5_avg_band;

queries.title: How much do venue and FPL's fixture difficulty rating (FDR) move points? Single-fixture gameweeks only, players who started.
queries.sql:
-- Q: How much do venue and FPL's fixture difficulty rating (FDR) move points?
-- Single-fixture gameweeks only, players who started.
SELECT p.position,
       CASE WHEN pm.was_home = 1 THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS venue,
       CASE WHEN pm.was_home = 1 THEN f.home_difficulty ELSE f.away_difficulty END AS fdr,
       COUNT(*)                               AS starts,
       ROUND(AVG(pm.total_points), 2)         AS avg_points,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(pm.clean_sheets), 1) AS clean_sheet_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(pm.expected_goals + pm.expected_assists), 3) AS avg_xgi
FROM player_match pm
JOIN players  p ON p.season = pm.season AND p.player_id = pm.player_id
JOIN fixtures f ON f.season = pm.season AND f.fixture_id = pm.fixture_id
WHERE pm.starts = 1 AND p.position <> 'AM'
GROUP BY p.position, venue, fdr
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY p.position, venue, fdr;

queries.title: Who scored far more (or fewer) goals than their chances deserved? Big gaps between goals and xG tend to shrink the next season, which makes this a useful "buy low / sell high" signal.
queries.sql:
-- Q: Who scored far more (or fewer) goals than their chances deserved?
-- Big gaps between goals and xG tend to shrink the next season, which makes
-- this a useful "buy low / sell high" signal.
WITH season_xg AS (
    SELECT pm.season, p.player_code, p.web_name, p.position,
           SUM(pm.goals_scored)   AS goals,
           SUM(pm.expected_goals) AS xg,
           SUM(pm.minutes)        AS minutes
    FROM player_match pm
    JOIN players p ON p.season = pm.season AND p.player_id = pm.player_id
    -- 2022-23 is excluded: xG was only tracked from GW16 that season, so a
    -- full season of goals would be compared with half a season of xG.
    WHERE pm.season <> '2022-23'
    GROUP BY pm.season, p.player_code
    HAVING SUM(pm.expected_goals) >= 5
),
with_next AS (
    SELECT a.*,
           b.goals - b.xg AS next_season_gap,
           b.season       AS next_season
    FROM season_xg a
    LEFT JOIN season_xg b
      ON b.player_code = a.player_code
     AND b.season = CASE a.season WHEN '2022-23' THEN '2023-24'
                                  WHEN '2023-24' THEN '2024-25'
                                  WHEN '2024-25' THEN '2025-26' END
)
SELECT season, web_name, position, goals,
       ROUND(xg, 1)              AS xg,
       ROUND(goals - xg, 1)      AS goals_minus_xg,
       ROUND(next_season_gap, 1) AS next_season_goals_minus_xg,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY season ORDER BY goals - xg DESC) AS overperf_rank
FROM with_next
ORDER BY season, goals_minus_xg DESC;

queries.title: Did the 2025-26 "defensive contribution" scoring rule change which positions score? Share of all FPL points earned by each position, per season (starters only).
queries.sql:
-- Q: Did the 2025-26 "defensive contribution" scoring rule change which positions score?
-- Share of all FPL points earned by each position, per season (starters only).
WITH by_pos AS (
    SELECT pm.season, p.position,
           SUM(pm.total_points) AS points,
           SUM(pm.minutes)      AS minutes
    FROM player_match pm
    JOIN players p ON p.season = pm.season AND p.player_id = pm.player_id
    WHERE p.position <> 'AM'
    GROUP BY pm.season, p.position
)
SELECT season, position,
       points,
       ROUND(100.0 * points / SUM(points) OVER (PARTITION BY season), 1) AS share_of_points_pct,
       ROUND(90.0 * points / minutes, 2)                                AS points_per_90
FROM by_pos
ORDER BY position, season;
